key_insight: A2D2 enables reward-guided fine-tuning of any-length discrete diffusion models by jointly optimizing insertion and unmasking policies, so decoding can adapt to sequence length while targeting higher-quality outputs.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical training-and-inference framework for sequence generators where fixed-length decoding is too restrictive, improving flexibility, accuracy, and reward optimization.
method: Derives the Radon-Nikodym derivative for the joint insertion–unmasking path measure.
Introduces Adaptive Joint Decoding (AJD), a quality-based inference schedule with a provably optimal path measure.
Uses tractable insertion and unmasking quality objectives to minimize decoding error without target samples.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports empirical gains in reward optimization, generation flexibility, and accuracy over prior fixed-length fine-tuning and inference-time guidance methods.
watch_item: The approach depends on estimating insertion/unmasking quality and implementing the joint path objective correctly, which may add optimization complexity and tuning sensitivity.
paper_title: A2D2: Fine-Tuning Any-Length Discrete Diffusion for Adaptive Decoding
